key_insight: A stronger teacher does not automatically produce a better distilled model: the critic must also be capable enough to provide reliable guidance. Experiments show that increasing teacher size while keeping a small critic fixed can hurt student quality and destabilize training.
problem_solved: Distribution Matching Distillation relies on an online critic to estimate the student distribution's score. An inadequate critic can make the training signal unreliable, limiting the benefits of a stronger teacher.
method: Train a few-step student using the difference between the teacher's score and the critic's estimate of the student distribution's score.
Run controlled experiments across seven SiT model sizes on ImageNet to examine teacher–critic capacity balance.
Investigate critic capacity and information needs; the provided abstract is truncated before the information-side findings.
impact: Practitioners should consider critic capacity alongside teacher size when designing distillation systems. Scaling the teacher alone can waste compute and reduce student quality.

paper_title: A Better Critic Matters for Distribution Matching Distillation
paper_authors: Zongze Wu, Xianbang Wang, Zhengyang Geng, Mingdeng Cao, Zhoutong Zhang
